summary: The legal timer window permits at most seventeen invocations; correctness depends on the immediate call, fixed interval cadence, argument forwarding, cancellation safety, and finite timer cleanup rather than scalable wall-clock growth.

workload_bound.source_constraint: 30 <= t <= 100 and 10 <= cancelTimeMs <= 500, including the immediate call

replacement_checks.evidence: One function call occurs immediately, one interval handle is created, and each of the k timer firings performs one invocation before a constant-time clearInterval cancellation.
Authored schedules cover cancellation before the first repeat, one repeat, all three official arities, negative and zero results, and the maximum seventeen invocations.
The deterministic adapter records every scheduled time and return value so cases verify time zero, exact t-spaced cadence, argument spreading, and absence of calls at or after cancellation.
The exact native timer source is remotely Accepted under the provider timeout, and every authored schedule terminates at a finite cancellation time.
